title: Historical joint scenarios gave no clear low-tail score gain for NRCS runoff errors at 221 sites in 2016-2025
abstract: We tested historical scenarios for joint NRCS April-July runoff forecast errors at 221 points in five western drainage regions. For each year in 2016-2025, earlier annual regional error fractions formed two distributions: coherent years and independent regional years. Both had identical regional marginals and expected network shares. Exact CRPS enumeration gave a 0.37% low-tail score reduction from coherent years, with a conditional 95% whole-year interval of -8.72% to +4.48%. Fixed-history and site-weight tests also gave no clear gain. Low-tail shares in 2021 and 2025 exceeded every earlier coherent scenario. A full-record dependence excess therefore did not establish forecast benefit from this historical template. Upper-tail gains were larger but uncertain, and threshold scores could worsen. The method cannot create new joint extremes or repair changing marginal errors. Ten test years, a selected complete panel, revised final forecasts and adjusted volumes limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, aggregate evidence and a separate score check are supplied. Raw source records remain external.

display.caption: Forward scenario forecasts and score gains. Keeping historical years together gave no clear low-tail gain; all methods use earlier years only.
